text: It falls back to the Echo instance's logger: at the end of the middleware, if `config.Output == nil` the line is written with `c.Logger().Output().Write(buf.Bytes())` (middleware/logger.go:215-218). Note that `DefaultLoggerConfig.Output` is itself nil, so the "Default value os.Stdout" documented on the field is achieved by this fallback — the log goes to the request's Echo logger output, which is os.Stdout unless you changed it (e.g. `e.Logger.SetOutput(...)`).

Found it: with a balancer that has no targets, `Next()` indexes an empty slice and panics (index out of range) instead of degrading gracefully. I'll make both balancers return nil when there are no targets and have the proxy middleware answer with 503 Service Unavailable. ETA ~3 min.

It returns a 500 error: `echo.NewHTTPError(http.StatusInternalServerError, i.(error).Error())` (middleware/decompress.go:94-97) — i.e. it assumes the non-`*gzip.Reader` value is an `error` and uses its message. Note the assertion `i.(error)` is unchecked, so if the pool ever returned something that is neither a `*gzip.Reader` nor an `error` (e.g. nil), that line would panic rather than return an error.

Fixed and checked. In middleware/proxy.go: both `randomBalancer.Next` and `roundRobinBalancer.Next` now return nil when the balancer has no targets (instead of panicking with index out of range), and `ProxyWithConfig` returns `echo.ErrServiceUnavailable` (503) when the balancer yields no target. Verified with a temporary test: empty round-robin, empty random and a custom nil-returning balancer all give 503 instead of panicking. The full suite (`go test -race ./...`) still passes.

`MethodOverride()` returns an `echo.MiddlewareFunc` — specifically `MethodOverrideWithConfig(DefaultMethodOverrideConfig)`. That middleware checks the request for an overridden method (by default from the `X-HTTP-Method-Override` header) and, only for `POST` requests, replaces `req.Method` with it before calling the next handler.
